passage: Friday. During the match today somebody shouted insults at me on voice chat. My face went hot, my hands shook on the controller and I typed half a nasty reply 😠. Then I deleted it. I muted him and blocked him. Damini, my sister, was sitting next to me and said, "Show Mama." I didn't want to, but I did. Mama said she was sorry that happened and that I handled it well by not answering him. My chest is still a bit tight. I think the match was ruined, but I'm okay. - Tanvir

qa.q: What did Tanvir do to the player who shouted at him?
qa.a: He muted him and blocked him.

qa.q: How did Tanvir feel on being shouted at, and what did Tanvir want to do?
qa.a: Tanvir felt angry and upset: Tanvir's face went hot, hands shook, and Tanvir typed half a nasty reply before deleting it.

qa.q: Why is muting and blocking wiser than trading insults?
qa.a: Insults would only feed the shouting, while muting and blocking end it and telling Mama brings support.

qa.q: How might Damini have seen the moment beside Tanvir?
qa.a: Damini was probably worried for Tanvir and wanted Tanvir to get help, which is why she said to show Mama.

grounding: Illustrates a child insulted in an online game who feels the urge to hit back but mutes, blocks and tells a parent.
